subject: Request: tenant-scoped log retention exception - NovaLabs
messages:
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@novalabs.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-scoped log retention exception request

Hi Soojin / Monica,

Quick one from NovaLabs legal/ops: during a recent compliance review they flagged that our debugging traces contain PII-like identifiers for a subset of sessions. We need to request a temporary, tenant-scoped retention exception so that NovaLabs can retain full-session debug traces for 180 days (our default is 30) for three tenant IDs while we run a parallel validation and redaction effort.

Ask: can Redwood provide a scoped exception limited to tenant IDs TL-44, TL-67, TL-93, with the following constraints:
- Only the raw debug traces for those tenants are retained 180 days; all other tenants remain on standard TTL.
- Access to retained traces must be logged and restricted to a named NovaLabs security group (legal@novalabs.com will provide accounts).
- Redwood must provide an evidence package (SOC 2 control maps + export of the retention rule configuration) that NovaLabs can include in their audit.

Timeline: we need confirmation of feasibility and a sample evidence bundle by 2028-03-20. Procurement will follow with a PO/contract amendment if feasible.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Security Operations, NovaLabs
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@novalabs.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-scoped log retention exception request

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask. We can support tenant-scoped retention windows as an exceptional workflow; a few pragmatic notes and next steps: 

1) Scope & controls: we can scope a 180-day TTL to the three tenant IDs you listed. We will apply a named retention rule that is auditable (rule id and effective timestamp).

2) Access gating: Redwood can restrict access to retained traces via RBAC groups. We will need the list of Redwood user emails (or sso groups) that NovaLabs wants granted read access. Best practice is to use SSO group mapping rather than listing individual accounts.

3) Evidence pack: I am attaching a short process overview (scoped-retention-process.pdf) that describes how the rule is implemented, the audit trail we capture, and the export you can use for audit evidence.

4) Controls and compensating measures: because this is a deviation from standard TTL, we recommend encrypting retained artifacts with a tenant-specific KMS key and enabling extra logging to your supplied SIEM ingest. If you require, we can also provide a limited snapshot export showing the rule configuration and an internal SOC 2 control mapping (redlined-MSA-NovaLabs.pdf will contain proposed contract language changes).

Next actions: please confirm the precise account list or SSO group, and whether you want tenant-scoped KMS or Redwood-managed keys. Once confirmed, I'll coordinate with Jordan (ops) to schedule the change window and with Priyom (legal) for contract amendment language.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Security Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: scoped-retention-process.pdf (application/pdf, 78KB)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@novalabs.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-scoped log retention exception request — contract and evidence

Hi Sam — looping in legal/cust success items and sending an initial evidentiary bundle.

- I've attached a redlined MSA that includes a limited TTL carveout clause and suggested language around access controls (redlined-MSA-NovaLabs.pdf).
- Also attached: SOC 2 summary and an index of evidence artifacts we can produce (SOC2-summary-2027.pdf). The index lists the control IDs and sample exports (audit logs, retention-rule JSON, KMS key metadata).

A few clarifications before we proceed to DocuSign: 
1) KMS: if you elect tenant-specific customer-managed keys (CMK), we will need key ARNs and confirmation of key rotation policy. CMKs add time to provisioning; Redwood-managed tenant key is the faster path.
2) Audit export frequency: we can provide a one-time snapshot of the retention-rule config and a 30‑day rolling export of the access logs, or can set up automated weekly exports if you prefer.
3) Amendment timeline: given internal approvals, we estimate 3 business days to configure the scoped rule once accounts and KMS decisions are finalized.

If NovaLabs confirms CMK choice or Redwood-managed key, and provides the SSO group/members, I will prepare a DocuSign amendment and routing instructions.

—Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined-MSA-NovaLabs.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB); SOC2-summary-2027.pdf (application/pdf, 245KB)
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@novalabs.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: legal@novalabs.com
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-scoped log retention exception request — contract and evidence

Thanks — this looks good. NovaLabs confirms:
- We accept Redwood-managed keys for this pilot (to keep timeline short).
- SSO group: NL-SEC-DEBUG (we will send the SCIM group mapping and members to monica@redwood.com).
- We want weekly audit exports to start on the first full week after rule activation.

Please proceed with the DocuSign amendment. Procurement will issue PO #PO-202803-NL once the amendment is in place. We appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Security Operations, NovaLabs

Note: Sam attaches a PO stub in a later procurement thread — not included in this security thread.
